correctness.rationale: The support function of centrally symmetric root polytope Q_{p,q} is max_cross |U_i-U_j|, hence full width=2 times this gap. Conditioning on unordered coordinates randomizes the labelled p-subset uniformly. For any real numbers z_i and t>=0, two far-pair edges must be linked by an edge connecting an appropriate extreme endpoint, so all far edges share exactly one nontrivial connected component of s vertices; no edges gives s=0. A partition avoids crossings iff this whole component is monochromatic, probability [C(p,s)+C(q,s)]/C(n,s), with s=0 probability1. Balancing p→p+1 yields difference [C(p,s-1)-C(q-1,s-1)]/C(n,s)≤0 for q>=p+2, yielding every threshold weak dominance. For almost every direction coordinates are distinct; t strictly between the largest second gap and the total range yields exactly the one edge joining extrema s=2, so each positive-moment survival integral increases strictly. Independently counted all uniform bipartitions in 18 threshold/part instances and recovered the exact conditional formula. Finite checks are not used to prove general n or Haar directions.
residual_risks: The deterministic component lemma is valid for strict >t, including coincident z; strict inequality uses almost-sure distinct coordinates.
No pointwise width comparison for one chosen fixed direction is asserted.

value.rationale: The full first-order stochastic ordering of intrinsic metric widths for nonnested complete-bipartite symmetric edge polytopes is a geometric strengthening far beyond one mean or Ehrhart invariant.
